You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Status of Seller material:** These are counterparty drafts. I have reviewed them as negotiating positions, not as agreed terms.

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim

The Seller's preamble says these positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL" and "are not intended to be re-opened." It also calls 10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers "standard and widely accepted market terms."

**My advice is not to accept this framing.**
- **No recorded authority.** Our playbook records no written authority from Amelia Frost for either the 20% cap fallback or the 18-month fallback. Both require written approval identifying the specific draft. A Seller's description of what principals agreed is not that authority.
- **Unsupported market claims.** The market-practice assertions are advocacy with no data behind them, and they do not bind us.
- **Recommended action.** Before the mark-up goes out, confirm with Amelia Frost directly whether she has had any principal-level discussion. If she has not, the cover note should say plainly that no position in this draft is agreed, and that the Buyer's mark-up is the next turn of a live negotiation.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m proposed, against our 25% / AUD 6.0m
- **Departure:** The Seller has opened at our *conditional fallback*. That fallback is unavailable without Amelia Frost's written authority, and none has been given.
- **Push back:** Restore 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is reachable.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2)

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Basket mechanism | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar once exceeded (tipping) |

- **Why it matters:** Together these are a significant erosion of the warranty package. A AUD 25k de minimis would knock out many individually modest but real claims, such as individual supplier, employee or customer issues. A AUD 250k *deductible* means we would absorb the first quarter-million permanently.
- **Push back:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000 on a tipping basis. Add an aggregation rule so that claims from the same or related facts count as one claim for de minimis purposes. Otherwise a series of related issues, such as the three Sandbar renewals of AUD 110k each, could be argued apart.

### 1.3 General claims period (cl 12.3/13): 18 months proposed, against our 24 months
- This is again our fallback, which needs Amelia Frost's written approval that has not been given.
- **Push back:** 24 months after Completion.

### 1.4 Hidden override (cl 12.3/13): "any limitation… applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- **This is a structural trap.** It flips the default so that every limitation reaches every category of claim: Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants. Any category we forget to carve out expressly would fall under the general regime by default.
- **Push back:** Delete it. Instead, the general limitations should apply **only** to "General Warranty Claims" as a defined term. Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations (price, adjustments, Debt repayment) and covenant breaches should each sit in their own regime. Add an express clause that nothing in the general limitation provisions limits those other categories.

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title folded into the general regime
- **Departure:** The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the same 20% cap and 18-month period "for administrative simplicity."
- **Why it matters:** Title is the thing we are buying. If title fails, our loss is the whole price, not 20% of it.
- **Push back:** Fundamental/Title warranties should have:
  - a cap of 100% of the price;
  - a claims period of at least six years; and
  - no application of the general basket, de minimis or any knowledge bar.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **The draft contains no fraud carve-out.** Read with 1.4, it would purport to cap, time-bar and exclude reliance-based claims for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Push back (non-negotiable):** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. The carve-out should cover the Seller and its officers, employees, agents and advisers. Our playbook says no one may waive this, so it is not a trading chip. Also check that the entire-agreement and non-reliance clauses do not try to exclude statutory misleading-conduct remedies beyond what is enforceable, and that the fraud carve-out expressly overrides them.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2)
- **What it says:** §1.1 discloses everything "contained or referred to" in the whole data room as at 22 September 2026. §1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Why it matters:** This would let the Seller defend almost any warranty claim by pointing to a document somewhere in the data room, or to anything a public search could have found. It empties the warranties.
- **Push back:** Delete §1.1 and §1.2. Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed** against a particular warranty in the Disclosure Letter should qualify the warranties. "Fairly" means with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. There should be no deemed disclosure of the data room, public registers or matters a prudent search would reveal.
- **§1.4 (non-admission):** This is broadly acceptable. However, the SPA should state that it does not dilute the Seller's covenants or conditions. For example, the Bluefen consent and the Riverlark discharge must still be delivered regardless of §1.4.
- **Staleness:** The letter is dated as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Require an updated Disclosure Letter for signing and a bring-down at Completion. Material changes since then should be disclosed specifically and should not cure warranties silently.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **What it says:** No claim for any matter "of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Why it matters:** It is drafted as broadly as possible. It imputes our advisers' knowledge to us and covers anything "discoverable," whether or not anyone actually knew it. In effect it reintroduces the general disclosure we are rejecting in 2.1.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. State expressly that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge of the Buyer or its advisers.
- **Separately:** Where any warranty is qualified by *Seller* knowledge, the knowledge should be that of named Seller knowledge persons, having made reasonable enquiry. No knowledge qualifier should ever excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Specific transaction issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002; DL §2)
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, or roughly 30%. DD-002 cl 11.2 contains a change-control consent with conditions in cl 11.3. The Seller's own letter confirms there is **no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.**
- **Seller position:** "Reasonable endeavours," with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- **Why it matters:** A consent can be delivered without its cl 11.3 conditions being met, which could leave the consent ineffective or open to challenge. Losing about 30% of revenue would strike at the valuation. For a customer this material, reasonable endeavours alone is not enough.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a **Condition Precedent**, for the Buyer's benefit and waivable only by the Buyer. It is satisfied only when the Bluefen consent is effective **and** there is evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that every cl 11.3 condition has been met.
  - Delete "deemed satisfied on delivery."
  - Strengthen the obligation from reasonable endeavours. Add a Buyer right to review drafts of the consent request and the consent, and an obligation to keep us informed.
  - Give the Buyer a right to terminate if the condition is not satisfied by the end date.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DD-003; DL §3)
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. DD-003 has a change-control provision (cl 8.1) and a discharge provision (cl 9.2). The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Seller position:** A release "following Completion."
- **Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. If we pay the price before Riverlark's security is released, Paperbark could be in default under cl 8.1 at the moment of Completion, and the security could remain over company assets after we own it. We also need to check DD-003 for any security over the **shares themselves**. If there is any, it also goes to title (see 3.8).
- **Push back:**
  - Require a current payout letter from Riverlark that states the daily rate.
  - Repay Riverlark **directly from Completion funds** as a funds-flow line item, treated as Debt in the price mechanics.
  - Obtain effective security releases at Completion: a deed of release, PPSR discharges, and return of any title documents.
  - A post-Completion release is acceptable **only** with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither has been offered, so do not concede this.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses (Funds flow; DD-005; DL §5)
- **Facts:** There are AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses. The Seller confirms they are **not** in the funds flow, describes them as "a matter for the Seller," and does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Why it matters:** These are company liabilities that the Completion event triggers. If they sit outside the funds flow, the Company, and so the Buyer, pays them after Completion while the price stays unchanged. "A matter for the Seller" is not an enforceable funding mechanism. This is the kind of silent exclusion the playbook targets.
- **Push back:**
  - Include the AUD 420,000 **plus all triggered on-costs** (payroll tax, superannuation, any PAYG and other employer costs) as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Costs. Alternatively, require the Seller to fund it expressly.
  - Back this with a specific indemnity, and require the Seller to confirm the on-cost position.
  - I have not quantified the on-costs. We need the Seller's calculation, which our payroll and tax advisers should check.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; DL §4)
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. The Seller itself notes this is not bank verification of non-payment. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
- **Why it matters:** The risk is not just the AUD 180k. If ownership of the SOW3 materials has not passed, Paperbark may not own IP it uses, and Ironquay could assert rights or bring infringement claims. A payment-only indemnity does not cover that.
- **Our position on the AUD 180k:** We should not assume it is owed, and we should not assume it is paid. Neither has been independently verified.
- **Push back:**
  - **Preserve the cure.** Require evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees, or settlement through the funds flow, plus an executed confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable.
  - **Broaden the indemnity** to cover any failure of SOW3 IP to vest in the Company, any Ironquay claim (fees, interest, IP or injunctive relief), and third-party infringement claims arising from SOW3 materials. It should sit outside the general cap, basket and time limit.
  - **Leave the IP warranty terms open.** Do not accept them as "settled" (see 3.7).

### 3.5 Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006; DL §6)
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). It is not established whether the file was accessed, what the exact scope is, or whether notification is required. The investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller position:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Our position:** We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification obligation or quantified loss. By the same token, we should not accept the Seller's assurance that the matter is immaterial. Its own disclosure says the facts are not established.
- **Push back:**
  - Add pre-Completion covenants to preserve all relevant logs (email, access and download logs, link-access records), complete a proper investigation, give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings, and consult the Buyer before any notification decision or regulator or customer communication.
  - Draft no warranty or recital that characterises the incident as immaterial.
  - Seek specific protection, such as a specific indemnity, for losses from the incident, including any notification, remediation or regulatory costs if those obligations turn out to arise. Do not attach a number to it.
  - Ask for an updated status. Six weeks have passed since 22 September.

### 3.6 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL §8)
- **Facts:** There are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each, AUD 330,000 in total. The Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure itself does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Our position:** We should not classify these as Debt or seek a price deduction automatically. We also should not accept the "ordinary course" label on the Seller's word.
- **Action:** Diligence questions to the Seller:
  - Why are there three related renewals, and what are their timing and scope?
  - Are they committed, terminable, or prepaid or accrued?
  - Do they fall in or out of the locked/accounts period?
  - Were they entered into outside normal practice, for example around the sale process?

  The answers will tell us whether any element should be treated as Debt or covered by a specific warranty. Make sure the aggregation rule in 1.2 stops them being split below the de minimis.

### 3.7 Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller position:** "Settled under the general regime above."
- **Our position:** These terms are **open**. Do not accept that they are settled, and do not let them fall under the general regime by default (see 1.4). Keep Tax (including a tax indemnity and its own time limit) and IP as separately negotiated categories. Do not assume unlimited liability is available, and do not assume any position has been resolved.

### 3.8 Title (DD-012; DL §10)
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **Why it is insufficient:** DD-012 is an internal record supplied by the Seller. The Seller's own letter confirms the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, freedom from encumbrances and authority. This includes:
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates;
  - the issue and transfer history, supported by allotment and transfer documents;
  - PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company, plus confirmation that no share security exists (cross-check Riverlark DD-003);
  - the Company constitution and any shareholders' agreement (for pre-emption or other restrictions); and
  - Seller board resolutions authorising the sale.

  Back this with Fundamental warranties on the 100% / six-year terms in 1.5.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority
- These are not covered by the playbook. The Seller's letter describes the lease as notification-only and the Mossvale clause as an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale.
- **Action:** Have our team check both against the underlying documents rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation. Make sure any lease notification is given in time, as a Completion deliverable if it is a pre-Completion obligation, and confirm there is no change-of-control trigger in either document.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "FINAL / agreed at principal level" | Not to be re-opened | Reject. Confirm with Amelia Frost. No written authority exists |
| 2 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (20% needs Amelia's written authority, not given) |
| 3 | De minimis / basket | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar**, plus aggregation of related claims |
| 4 | General claims period | 18 months | **24 months** (18 needs Amelia's written approval, not given) |
| 5 | "Limitations apply to all Claims unless stated" | Default override | **Delete.** General limits apply to General Warranty Claims only, with categories kept separate |
| 6 | Title / capacity | General cap and period | **100% cap, ≥6 years**, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge |
| 7 | Limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance for "all Claims" | No fraud carve-out | **Non-negotiable fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out** from everything |
| 8 | Disclosure | Whole data room, registers, public records | **Specific fair disclosure only**. Updated letter and bring-down |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Blanket, includes advisers and "discoverable" | **Delete**. Seller knowledge only via named persons plus reasonable enquiry |
| 10 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours, satisfied on delivery | **Buyer-waivable CP: effective consent plus evidence cl 11.3 conditions met** |
| 11 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion** |
| 12 | DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k) | Outside funds flow | **Line item plus on-costs**, or seller-funded with indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay | Payment-only indemnity | **Broaden to IP vesting and claims. Preserve SOW3 cure** (payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment). AUD 180k unverified |
| 14 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, updates, consultation, specific protection.** No assumption of breach or quantum |
| 15 | Sandbar (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | **Diligence first.** No automatic Debt or deduction |
| 16 | Tax / IP | "Settled" under general regime | **Open.** Separate regimes. No assumption of unlimited liability |
| 17 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence**: ASIC, certificates, PPSR, resolutions, transfer history |
| 18 | Lease / Mossvale | No consent needed | Verify against documents. Handle notification timing |

**Suggested priority for the mark-up:**
1. **Must-haves:** the fraud carve-out, deletion of the default override in 1.4, the separate Title regime, and deletion of general disclosure and buyer knowledge.
2. **Completion mechanics with real money attached:** Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses.
3. **The economic terms:** cap, thresholds and claims period, held at our starting positions.
4. **Remaining items:** the Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar protections and diligence requests.

**Internal escalation:** If the deal team wants to use either fallback (the 20% cap or 18 months) at any point, get Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft first. Until then, hold our starting positions.
=== END ADVICE ===
